s4.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension

raw.champion: Renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension
raw.rationale: The presence of a right renal mass with areas of fat attenuation, a defect in the renal parenchyma, and visible vessels extending into the renal cortex, along with a fatty tumor thrombus within the right renal vein extending to the inferior vena cava, are characteristic findings of renal cell carcinoma with vascular extension.

rejected.label: Angiomyolipoma with renal vein thrombosis
rejected.why: While angiomyolipomas can contain fat and have vascular components, the presence of a tumor thrombus in the renal vein is more suggestive of a malignant process like renal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Renal metastasis from endometrial carcinoma
rejected.why: The primary tumor in the kidney and the presence of a fatty tumor thrombus are not typical for metastatic disease from endometrial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma with renal metastasis
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are rare and the described findings are more consistent with a primary renal tumor rather than a metastasis.

rejected.label: Leiomyosarcoma of the renal vein
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that would not typically present with a renal mass and fatty thrombus in the renal vein.

rejected.label: Renal vein leiomyomatosis
rejected.why: This condition involves benign smooth muscle growths in the renal vein and does not typically present with a renal mass or fatty attenuation.

rejected.label: Clear cell sarcoma of the kidney
rejected.why: This is a rare tumor that typically affects children and the described findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Renal medullary carcinoma
rejected.why: This is a rare and aggressive tumor that typically affects younger individuals with sickle cell trait and the described findings are not consistent with this diagnosis.
